reason: I want to start assembling the digestive system, and the salivary glands connect at the beginning of the tube.
expectation: The salivary glands will fit onto the digestive tube, probably leaving the other slots open.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting starch digestion, but assembling the organs first seems like a clear place to begin.

effect: The salivary glands fitted as expected, so I’ll continue adding the digestive organs.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, though it did not yet explain what the glands contribute.
reason: The pancreas has a duct leading to the small intestine, so fitting it advances the assembly goal.
expectation: The pancreas will fit into its marked slot, leaving the liver and gallbladder and portal vessel slots open.

alternatives.reason: The liver and gallbladder also fit the assembly goal, but I chose the pancreas first.

effect: The pancreas fitted as expected, so I’ll add the remaining available organs.
reaction: Another straightforward fitting; its role has not yet been explained.
reason: The liver and gallbladder are the remaining available organs for the assembly goal.
expectation: They will fit into the digestive tube, with the portal vessel slot still open.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting starch digestion, but want to finish the available organ fittings first.

effect: The organ-fitting goal is complete, and the result explains what each organ contributes. I’ll start breaking down the meal.
reaction: The explanation makes the earlier fittings more meaningful.
reason: Salivary amylase begins starch digestion, so this follows the explanation just given.
expectation: The amylase will break the starch into smaller pieces, possibly requiring further digestion.

alternatives.reason: Fat digestion also advances the goal, but I want to follow the starch route first.

effect: The starch became shorter chains, so it needs further breakdown for absorption.
reaction: The result was predictable but makes the stages of starch digestion clear.
reason: I’ll continue the starch route with the available digestive enzymes.
expectation: The enzymes will break the shorter chains into smaller sugars suitable for absorption.

alternatives.reason: Protein digestion also advances the goal, but I want to finish the starch route first.

effect: The starch route produced individual glucose molecules that can cross the intestinal lining, so I’ll move on to another part of the meal.
reaction: The result clearly connects starch breakdown to absorption.
reason: Protein-digesting enzymes should break the protein food into smaller pieces for absorption.
expectation: I expect smaller protein fragments or amino acids, though further digestion may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Fat also needs digestion, but I chose to follow the protein route first.

effect: Protein digestion produced amino acids, leaving fat digestion as the available meal breakdown action.
reaction: The result is clear, though it gives little detail about the breakdown.
reason: This is the only available combination and should advance the meal digestion goal.
expectation: Bile and lipase will help break the fat into smaller products suitable for absorption.

effect: Fat digestion completed the remaining goal. The result clarified that bile disperses fat while lipase breaks it apart.
reaction: The distinction between bile and lipase was useful and more informative than I expected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Breaking down fat was most worthwhile because the result distinguished the roles of bile and lipase, including that bile is not an enzyme.

leastWorthwhile.text: The individual organ fittings felt repetitive at first because their contributions were only explained after the last fitting.

surprise.text: The fat result clarified that bile disperses fat into droplets rather than acting as an enzyme.

arbitrary.text: The fittings had clear locations, but their purpose was initially less clear; the later explanation connected them to digestion.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter to see how the digestion products cross the gut lining, although the predictable fittings made this chapter feel somewhat repetitive.
